A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FuseUNet work and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E. Text and rendered-page comparisons reveal no material gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original FuseUNet segmentation experiments on five datasets in Tables 3–4, with ablations in Section 4.3 and additional empirical results in Appendices D–E.

after.justification: v2 retains the original FuseUNet segmentation results in Tables 3–4, ablation results in Section 4.3, and supplementary empirical results in Appendices D–E.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3, Algorithm 1, and Appendix A retain the same adaptive multistep predictor-corrector procedure, nmODE components, and feature-fusion architecture.

E1.justification: Both versions use ACDC, KiTS23, MSD brain tumor, ISIC2017, and ISIC2018 for the same segmentation tasks. No dataset, population, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 3–4 retain identical comparator membership within each experiment, including nn-UNet, UNETR, and UltraLight VM-UNet as the corresponding backbones.

E3.justification: Five-fold 3D cross-validation, 2D evaluation metrics, backbone settings, and learning rates remain unchanged. The new FLOPs note identifies a unit-conversion error without reporting revised experimental procedures.

E4.justification: The fusion-order and memory-capacity ablations, their segmentation findings, and the Appendix E visual examples remain unchanged. The general FLOPs correction introduces no new or redesigned analysis.

E5.justification: Appendix D retains the same fold-level reporting and Table 12 statistical analysis, including standard deviations, standard errors, confidence intervals, t-statistics, and p-values. No uncertainty-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: The new page 9 note states that all reported FLOPs are underestimated by a factor of ten, substantially correcting absolute computational-cost results. For example, Table 3's 264.9 GFLOPs for FuseUNet on ACDC/KiTS corresponds to 2649 under this correction, although both PDFs still print 264.9. Segmentation scores, parameter counts, timings, and displayed rankings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Theorems 3.1–3.2 and A.1–A.7, equations, and Appendix C computational-cost expressions are unchanged. The numerical unit correction adds no mathematical derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about generalizable multiscale fusion, parameter efficiency, and preserved segmentation performance. The new note explicitly maintains the experimental conclusions.

C2.justification: v2 newly explains that the FLOPs scaling error preserves relative comparisons across models and configurations. Existing interpretations of segmentation quality and limitations concerning historical-state memory consumption remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents the unit-scaling issue encountered when using a 3D input in the FLOPs demo script and reports a corresponding GitHub repository correction. Hardware, hyperparameters, and other implementation disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, and research positioning are unchanged. Bibliography entries move because of the inserted note, without additions or removals.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short Post-publication Note (July 2025) between the Impact Statement and References, along with running-title text. The remaining narrative and appendix structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Running title headers are added on pages 2–17, and the new note reflows the bibliography across pages 9–11. Figures 1–9 and Tables 1–12 retain their designs and placements.

improvement.justification: The new note discloses the tenfold FLOPs error and supplies a correction factor, improving transparency about computational costs. The benefit is limited because the affected tables still show the original values, while the method, segmentation evidence, and conclusions remain unchanged.
